purpose: Execute the golden-master live-replay verification that T-MIG-010's execution_record left PENDING (honest gap (c)): the 16-case identity set (15 auth + health) from T-MIG-003, replayed against a booted v2 api on a real Postgres.

environment.api: SyllabAI/syllabai-v2 @ main 67639db + T-MIG-016 fixes (see fixes[]); booted UNMODIFIED at the driver level via apps/api default fetch handler (Bun.serve, real HTTP :8090)
environment.database: local PostgreSQL 17.11 + pgvector 0.8.0 (no-root deb unpack; cleartext-password hba on 127.0.0.1:54329; schema = T-MIG-002 baseline 0000_organic_mauler.sql + seeded roles table; ZERO production/Neon connections)
environment.driver_seam: The api's identity path uses @neondatabase/serverless Client (WebSocket transport). A FakeWebSocket (neonConfig.webSocketConstructor + globalThis.WebSocket) tunnels raw wire bytes to the local Postgres. With cleartext hba, the client's pipelined Startup+'p'+query burst is consumed natively — identical semantics to the real Neon proxy. No api code was altered for transport.
environment.capture_config_parity: SYLLABAI_TEACHER_JOIN_CODE deliberately UNSET (auth-register-teacher-no-joincode-403 was captured with the gate fail-closed); SYLLABAI_JWT_SECRET 32+ bytes; DATABASE_URL jdbc-free

fixes.finding: golden/runner.ts --target path used the byte-strict deepEqual, IGNORING each case's tolerate rules — every case carrying a volatile field (ApiError.timestamp) was permanently unpassable live. This is why the gate sat at 0/16 and is the false-failure mirror of the GOLDEN_MASTER §5 false-confidence trap.
fixes.fix: replayAgainst now diffs with deepEqualTolerant(body, actual, case.tolerate) — the same comparator the selftest always used.
fixes.classification: golden-gate infrastructure defect (T-MIG-003 lane), fixed by R0, unit-pin unaffected (selftest green)

fixes.finding: apps/api/src/routes/health.ts served the seed's bare {status:UP}; the frozen core serves {groups:[liveness,readiness],status:UP} per golden actuator-health-parity (justified:true). The seed header itself conceded the core shape; the route never caught up.
fixes.fix: route now serves the captured core shape; unit pin updated to the golden shape.
fixes.classification: genuine parity divergence (seed-era bug), exposed by the fixed comparator, fixed by R0

fixes.finding: @Email failure message: v2 said 'must be a valid email'; the core's Hibernate default (captured: auth-register-bad-email-400) is 'must be a well-formed email address'.
fixes.fix: packages/contracts email refine message pinned to the captured text; 3 unit pins updated to the captured expectation.
fixes.classification: genuine parity divergence (contracts lane, R1), fixed by R0 as out-of-fence micro-fix with this receipt

fixes.finding: FIRST-field selection on multi-field violations: the port trusted zod's schema order (email first); live capture proves Hibernate's traversal reports PASSWORD first in both missing-fields captures.
fixes.fix: validationMessage now ranks issues by the core's OBSERVED traversal order (password → email → rest in schema order), documented as evidence-only-updatable.
fixes.classification: genuine parity divergence (T-MIG-010 lane), fixed by R0; update-on-evidence doctrine recorded in code

fixes.finding: T-MIG-002 baseline SQL defects, confirmed on vanilla Postgres: (a) the entire 0000_organic_mauler.sql is wrapped in a /* */ 'uncomment to run' block — it applies NOTHING when executed as-is; (b) ~203 CREATE INDEX statements carry drizzle-pull operator-class artifacts (text_ops on uuid, timestamptz_ops on uuid, int4_ops on varchar, …) and fail on any Postgres; (c) the schema-only baseline lacks the roles seed rows the user_roles FK requires (STUDENT/TEACHER/ADMIN) — identity writes fail without them.
fixes.fix: not fixed here (T-MIG-002/R2 lane). Local workarounds used for verification: wrapper stripped, broken indexes skipped (tables all applied), roles seeded.
fixes.classification: filed for T-MIG-002 follow-up; blocks clean re-baselining and any fresh-environment boot

tier_a_verbatim.command: bun golden/runner.ts --target http://127.0.0.1:8090 (16-case identity subset, runner at 67639db + F-1 fix)
fails_classified: auth-login-success-200 — status 200 OK; body differs ONLY in accessToken + user.id, the two fields R6 scrubbed at capture (fixed dummy / stable fake). Tier B passes it redacting exactly those two fields.

auth-register-success-201 — 409 vs 201: the fixture user already exists when the alphabetical verbatim order runs (duplicate-email case precedes register-success); Tier B re-runs it first on clean state and it PASSES with a full-shape match modulo the scrubbed fields.

auth-me-with-bearer-200 — the fixture's Authorization header carries the scrubbed dummy token; 401 fail-closed is the CORRECT honest-api behaviour (no golden-cheat acceptance path exists). Tier B passes it substituting a live-issued bearer token.

tier_b_state_aware.harness: executes the 4 state/scrub cases in dependency order (register → duplicate → login → /me with live token), diffing with the runner's own redact() semantics; only capture-scrubbed volatile fields (accessToken, id) redacted, everything else byte-exact

results.union: 16/16 unique identity golden cases verified green

supporting_gates.unit: 119 pass / 0 fail / 4 skip (skip = Neon-branch integration tier, requires INTEGRATION_DATABASE_URL)

verdict: T-MIG-010 identity port REPLAYS GREEN against the full 16-case T-MIG-003 identity golden set. The acceptance bar (0/16 → 16/16) is met; 4 genuine defects (F-1..F-4) were found by the gate and fixed in this pass; F-5 filed for T-MIG-002.
honest_gaps: R-JWT cross-verify with a Java-issued token still requires a capture-side run (T-MIG-010 gap (d) unchanged; unit fixtures remain jjwt-semantics-by-construction).
Tier B redacts exactly the two capture-scrubbed volatile fields; no other tolerance was used anywhere.
Verification ran against local Postgres, not a Neon branch — SQL surface is identical Postgres; Neon-specific proxy behaviour is out of scope and unchanged by this task.
Known T-MIG-010 scope boundary unchanged: per-IP RateLimitFilter (M1) still unported.
